newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Minister seeks "good sense" deal to end TAP strike.
newsitem.headline: Minister seeks "good sense" deal to end TAP strike.

text.p: A government minister said he would seek a "good sense" deal to end a selective pilots' strike at TAP-Air Portugal, which entered a second day on Sunday, so that the state carrier can avoid sliding into bankruptcy.

"There has to be an agreement that is reasonable. There has to be an agreement that does not bankrupt TAP," Public Works Minister Joao Cravinho told TSF radio after returning from an official visit to Brazil.
"I am willing (to negotiate) with good faith. What is not negotiable is good sense," he added.

Cravinho, the minister responsible for TAP, lambasted the policy of the pilots' union under which pilots who fell ill on the eve of a flight refused to be substituted, grounding the flight and causing the airline to lose money.
Pilots are staging the strike to protest against what they say is TAP's inefficient organisation of their working hours.

Three flights, to Madeira, Barcelona and Dublin, had been cancelled on Sunday morning and three evening flights, to London, Madrid and Ponta Delgada in the Azores, were expected to be called off, TAP officials said.

A TAP official told Reuters on Saturday that five flights had been cancelled that day as pilots began their indefinite stoppage a few hours ahead of its expected launch at midnight (2300 GMT Saturday).
The pilots were continuing planned flights as normal but were not operating non-scheduled flights, officials said.
Cravinho said TAP was pressing ahead with plans to invest 800 million escudos ($4.3 million) to upgrade its computing system used to plan flights and pilots' working hours.
Airline officials have said the strike could affect at least 15 percent of TAP's flights and could cost the carrier at least three billion escudos in August.
Government officials have repeatedly warned that if the strike continues, the financial problems of the loss-making airline would worsen, leading to its eventual closure.
Cravinho said the strike jeopardised ongoing talks between TAP and other airlines for a possible strategic partnership.
"This incident is a grave threat to (reaching) an agreement," he said.
Government officials met representatives of the pilots' union on Sunday to try to resolve the dispute, TSF radio reported.
TAP and pilot union officials were not immediately available for comment.
In April, a two-day stoppage by TAP pilots over working hours grounded international flights and stranded some 14,000 passengers.
